lead.title: U.S. prepares new tariff action against China, EU and others
lead.deck: The Trump administration is expected to announce higher tariffs aimed at what officials describe as subsidized overproduction abroad, according to people familiar with the plan.
paragraphs: The Trump administration is preparing to raise tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and 14 other economies, according to two people familiar with the matter who spoke to The Associated Press. The expected move would widen a trade fight that has continued even after Republicans’ midterm losses, with the White House arguing that foreign subsidies are distorting manufacturing competition and worsening strains on U.S. industry.

The prospective action arrives as inflation remains elevated and affordability has become a dominant political issue. Any tariff increase would risk higher import costs for some businesses and consumers while also signaling that the administration intends to keep using trade penalties as an industrial-policy tool. China has been trying to rebalance its economy, but weak domestic demand has pushed more firms toward export markets, adding to friction with trading partners.

stories.title: Democrats clinch House majority of at least 259 seats
stories.deck: The party’s margin is its largest in the chamber since 1990, setting up divided government in Washington.
paragraphs: Democrats have clinched a House majority of at least 259 seats, The Associated Press reported Wednesday, giving the party its biggest chamber margin since 1990. The result follows earlier gains in the Senate and leaves President Donald Trump facing a Congress with broad investigative power and a larger opposition caucus than many expected after the election season.

Party leaders and lawmakers are now publicly debating how to balance oversight with cost-of-living issues. Centrist Democrats have urged the caucus to devote most of its effort to affordability legislation while still using subpoena power and committee authority to challenge the White House.
stories.new_development: The new development is that Democrats have now secured a House majority of at least 259 seats, a concrete expansion beyond earlier reports that they had merely won control of the chamber.

stories.title: U.S. consumer confidence jumps in November
stories.deck: The Conference Board survey showed a marked improvement as gas prices eased and election uncertainty faded.
paragraphs: Americans’ confidence in the economy rose sharply in November, according to a report highlighted by the Associated Press, with lower gasoline prices and the end of election-season uncertainty helping lift sentiment. The improvement comes even as inflation remains higher than policymakers and households would like.

Economists have cautioned that confidence surveys have been less reliable predictors of actual spending since the pandemic. Still, the rebound offers a notable counterpoint to persistent concerns about prices, especially after government data earlier this month showed inflation moving higher in October.

stories.title: Libyan army vows retaliation after officers die from Ukrainian drone attack
stories.deck: The deaths broaden attention on a conflict that Kyiv says reaches beyond Ukraine’s own territory.
paragraphs: Libya’s army said it would retaliate after two naval officers died from wounds suffered in a Ukrainian drone attack, according to the Associated Press. The episode adds another international dimension to the war as Ukraine continues to describe strikes on Russian assets and aligned forces beyond its borders.

The development follows recent claims by Kyiv that it had struck a Russian warship in Libya. It also lands as Russia’s war effort presses into another winter, with military, diplomatic and energy-security consequences extending well beyond Eastern Europe.
stories.new_development: The new development is Libya’s stated retaliation threat after two officers died of their wounds, moving the story beyond the initial report of the Ukrainian strike.

stories.title: North Korea orders closure of new Swiss diplomatic office
stories.deck: Pyongyang gave the senior Swiss diplomat 48 hours to leave, citing Swiss sanctions.
paragraphs: North Korea demanded the closure of Switzerland’s newly opened diplomatic office in Pyongyang and ordered its senior diplomat to depart within 48 hours, according to the Associated Press. State media linked the move to Swiss sanctions related to a children’s camp, turning a narrow dispute into a fresh diplomatic rupture.

The step underscores North Korea’s increasingly confrontational posture as it aligns more closely with Russia amid the war in Ukraine. Even limited diplomatic openings remain fragile, and Pyongyang’s decision quickly shut down one of the few recent signs of a small international thaw.

stories.title: Amnesty calls for war-crimes investigation into shelling in Tigray
stories.deck: The rights group says renewed fighting near the Eritrean border has put civilians at risk.
paragraphs: Amnesty International called for an independent war-crimes investigation into shelling of civilian neighborhoods in Ethiopia’s Tigray region, the Associated Press reported. Residents near the Eritrean border described military buildups and fears of a wider return to war.

Fighting resumed in September despite the November 2022 agreement that had ended the previous two-year conflict. The renewed instability raises the prospect of another humanitarian crisis in a region still marked by displacement and deep political mistrust.

stories.title: Philadelphia advances bill requiring long-term shift away from incinerators and landfills
stories.deck: City Council’s commerce committee backed legislation calling for 60% of city trash to be diverted over 20 years.
paragraphs: Philadelphia would have to steer 60% of its trash away from landfills and incinerators over the next 20 years under legislation advanced Monday by City Council’s Commerce Committee. The bill directs the city to develop a formal zero-waste plan over the next three years, including expanded use of composting and other disposal methods.

The measure follows last week’s committee vote blocking the Parker administration from entering a new contract with Reworld, the Chester incinerator that has long handled roughly a third of the city’s trash. Administration officials said the new bill largely codifies work already underway, while some environmental advocates argued it needs stronger accountability and more emphasis on reducing waste at the source.
stories.new_development: The new development is that Council has now advanced a broader zero-waste framework with a 60% diversion target, after the earlier fight over the Reworld contract.

stories.title: Thanksgiving parade closures set for Center City Philadelphia
stories.deck: Road restrictions begin Wednesday evening ahead of Thursday morning’s parade.
paragraphs: Philadelphia’s annual Thanksgiving Day parade returns Thursday morning, and major road closures are scheduled in and around Center City throughout the week. The Inquirer reported that temporary no-parking restrictions begin Wednesday evening along or near the parade route.

Transit riders were advised to check SEPTA service updates for day-of changes. The annual event is one of the city’s largest holiday-season gatherings and typically reshapes traffic patterns well before the first floats roll.

stories.title: Council hearing presses Philadelphia DHS after foster child’s death
stories.deck: Lawmakers questioned oversight failures following the death of 10-year-old Malayshia Allford.
paragraphs: Philadelphia City Council held a hearing on the Department of Human Services’ foster-care system after the death of 10-year-old Malayshia Allford, whose body was found in Lindenwold earlier this month. WHYY reported that lawmakers examined agency shortcomings and questioned DHS Commissioner Kimberly Ali about oversight and accountability.

The hearing is part of a widening official response that also includes other investigations into the case and the broader foster system. The proceedings did not resolve the underlying failures, but they added public pressure on city agencies to explain how the placement and monitoring process broke down.

stories.title: Gov. Sherrill signs order aimed at improving child literacy in New Jersey
stories.deck: The order directs the Education Department to produce a plan for more evidence-based classroom practices.
paragraphs: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill signed an executive order intended to improve student literacy, The Inquirer’s South Jersey report noted Tuesday. The order calls on the state Department of Education to produce a plan within 90 days for districts to use more evidence-based practices.

The move places literacy policy near the top of the new administration’s education agenda. It also begins a longer process in which districts and the state will have to translate broad policy language into teacher training, curriculum choices and local implementation.

stories.title: Moorestown parents say school bullying cases need stronger response
stories.deck: Parents told the board the district’s reporting and investigation process is falling short.
paragraphs: Parents in Moorestown told the local school board last week that bullying remains a serious problem and that the district’s response process needs improvement. According to The Inquirer, speakers argued that incidents are not being handled transparently enough and said stronger procedures are needed before the problem can be reduced.

District teachers and classroom quality were praised by several parents even as they criticized the current system. The dispute leaves the board under pressure to show whether reporting, investigation and communication practices will change.

stories.title: AI-linked stocks drag on markets again
stories.deck: World shares were mixed after another retreat in technology names tied to the artificial-intelligence boom.
paragraphs: Global stock markets were mixed Wednesday after a fresh round of selling in AI-related shares hit Wall Street, the Associated Press reported. The pullback came even as other parts of the market were steadier and new U.S. consumer-confidence data showed improved sentiment.

The divergence reflects a market still trying to reconcile strong long-term enthusiasm for AI with higher interest rates, inflation worries and company-specific volatility. Nvidia’s recent upheaval has kept the sector unusually sensitive to leadership and policy shocks.

stories.title: Australia passes online-safety law with steep penalties for tech firms
stories.deck: The legislation could expose major platforms to fines worth up to 5% of global revenue.
paragraphs: Australia’s Parliament passed a major online-safety law Wednesday that could impose multibillion-dollar penalties on technology companies that fail to prevent what the government calls foreseeable online harms. The Associated Press reported that the measure cleared the House after a Senate deal with the Greens.

Supporters cast the bill as a tougher response to platform failures, while critics warned that broadly defined harms could encourage over-removal of lawful speech. The law adds to a growing set of national efforts to force large internet companies to police content more aggressively.

stories.title: OpenAI posts new GPT-6.2 system card as model rollout expands
stories.deck: The company published updated safety documentation tied to GPT-6.2 in ChatGPT.
paragraphs: OpenAI has published a system card for GPT-6.2 in ChatGPT dated Nov. 23, adding fresh deployment-safety documentation as the company expands its latest model family. The document says GPT-6.2 is intended to be used under OpenAI’s usage policies and terms, while separate product notes list GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol among the company’s recent releases.

The release continues a recent pattern in which model launches are accompanied by public-facing safety summaries rather than only product announcements. For developers and enterprise buyers, that documentation has become part of how vendors signal risk controls, limitations and intended use.

stories.title: NOAA warns of stormy Thanksgiving travel on both coasts
stories.deck: Federal forecasters say an eastern coastal storm and a Pacific system could disrupt road and air travel.
paragraphs: NOAA said Thanksgiving week travel is likely to be disrupted by a powerful coastal storm affecting the eastern half of the country and a Pacific system bringing rain and mountain snow to the West. The agency’s Weather Prediction Center said the busiest travel days could coincide with showers, thunderstorms and deteriorating road conditions in multiple regions.

The federal warning does not guarantee severe local impacts in every corridor, but it does set a broad national frame for one of the year’s heaviest travel periods. Travelers across the Mid-Atlantic, Southeast and western mountains were advised to expect changing conditions.

stories.title: NOAA says Atlantic hurricane season stayed quiet while Pacific surged
stories.deck: The agency tied the contrast to a very strong El Niño as the 2026 season nears its official end.
paragraphs: NOAA said the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season was quieter than average, with 10 named storms through Nov. 24 compared with a long-term average of 14. At the same time, the eastern and central Pacific saw above-average activity, including two disasters in Hawaii, in what the agency described as a season shaped by a very strong El Niño.
The season officially ends Nov. 30. NOAA presented the split outcome as another example of how large climate patterns can suppress activity in one basin while amplifying it in another.

stories.title: NASA invites backyard astronomers to help spot kilonovae
stories.deck: A new public-science push asks amateurs to watch for the aftermath of neutron-star collisions.
paragraphs: NASA published a Nov. 24 feature encouraging amateur astronomers to help search for kilonovae, the brief flashes created when neutron stars collide. The agency said small-telescope observers can contribute to spotting some of the universe’s most violent and scientifically valuable events.

The article is less a breaking-news item than a fresh invitation into citizen science. It reflects NASA’s continuing effort to connect professional observatories with volunteer skywatchers who may help identify transient cosmic events quickly.

stories.title: Today’s sky note: galaxies colliding in the NGC 7771 Group
stories.deck: NASA’s Astronomy Picture of the Day highlights a slow-motion merger nearly 200 million light-years away.
paragraphs: NASA’s Astronomy Picture of the Day for Nov. 24 featured the NGC 7771 Group, a set of interacting galaxies in Pegasus roughly 200 million light-years from Earth. The accompanying explanation said repeated close passages will likely end in a single much larger galaxy over billions of years.

The image is a reminder that galaxy mergers are a normal part of cosmic evolution, not rare accidents. Astronomers study such systems in part to better understand the long-term future interaction between the Milky Way and Andromeda.

stories.title: Al Gore is buying a Tennessee local newspaper
stories.deck: The former vice president said the purchase is meant to preserve an independent local voice.
paragraphs: Former Vice President Al Gore is set to become the new owner of a local newspaper in Tennessee, according to the Associated Press. Gore said the move is intended to preserve an independent local news outlet in Carthage and Smith County as closures and consolidation continue across the industry.

The purchase stands out both because of Gore’s national profile and because newspaper ownership has increasingly shifted away from locally rooted hands. In a period of shrinking local-news capacity, the deal lands as an unusual vote for small-town print journalism.

stories.title: Melania Trump says another group of Ukrainian and Russian children has been reunited with families
stories.deck: The first lady’s office said this is the seventh such group connected to her effort.
paragraphs: Melania Trump said a seventh group of Ukrainian and Russian children has been reunited with their families through an initiative tied to her office, according to the Associated Press. The announcement was framed around children caught up in a war they did not choose.

Whatever the politics surrounding the broader conflict, the episode is one of the few war-related stories centered on family restoration rather than battlefield movement. The report did not suggest a wider settlement, but it did point to one narrow humanitarian channel still functioning.

stories.title: Trail Blazers hand 76ers a 128-111 loss
stories.deck: Portland snapped Philadelphia’s five-game winning streak on Monday night.
paragraphs: Portland beat Philadelphia 128-111 on Monday, Nov. 23, with Deni Avdija scoring 31 points, according to NBA.com’s game summary. The loss dropped the 76ers to 14-4 and ended a five-game winning streak.
The game turned on Portland’s outside shooting and a strong second half after a close opening stretch. Philadelphia was back on the schedule Wednesday against Miami.

long_reads.title: OpenAI product releases and safety documentation
long_reads.description: For readers tracking the AI industry, OpenAI’s recent product-release list and GPT-6.2 safety documentation show how vendors are pairing launches with more formal public risk disclosures.
